# Rung M: `Maybe`, `Just` and `Nothing` for the compiler world

problem: `explorations/compile-ladder/after/raw/tests/oddJuxt.fss.compile:2` — "Function Nothing is not defined."; 472 further occurrences of "Maybe is undefined." across the ladder's recorded first errors, and the compiler prelude declares none of the three names.
spec: `Specification/basic-lib/convenience.tex:33-55` — the Convenience Types section declares `trait Maybe[\T\] comprises { Nothing, Just[\T\] }` with `isNothing: Boolean`, `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}`, and `object Just[\T\](just: T) extends Maybe[\T\]`; used at `Specification/basic/exceptions.tex:112-130`, which writes the defaults of two `Maybe` fields as `= Nothing`.
precedent: `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649-661` with bodies at `.fss:1308-1367` — the shipped `value trait Option[\E19\] extends { Condition[\E19\] } comprises { NoneObject[\E19\], Some[\E19\] }` with `coerce(_: None)` and `value object None end`, which is this protocol under other names and is the shape copied member for member; the team's own commented draft for these names is `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229`.
deviation: eight, each listed in §6 below; the first is that the specification's single non-parametric `Nothing` is realised as `NothingObject[\T\]` plus `value object Nothing end` plus `coerce(_: Nothing)`, because a `where` clause on an object declaration is refused by `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:4088` (`forObjectDeclPrePass`, `header.getWhereClause().isNone()`), while coercion is the one mechanism this path has and the interpreter lacks.

## 1. What was inherited

Nothing. `git log --oneline cb242a2d8..HEAD` was empty and `git status --short` clean when this rung started, so there was no earlier attempt to verify; `tmp/` held no logs. Every check below was run in this worktree.

## 2. Where does this fix belong

`explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:332` is the `Maybe` row: interpreter at `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:813-880`, compiler world "present at `CompilerLibrary.fsi:194-204` but wholly commented out; `CompilerBuiltin.fsi:648-660` ships `Option`/`Some`/`NoneObject` instead". The row's spec column names `library/default-libraries.tex`, which is an api rendering and therefore not evidence (`Specification/library/structure.tex:25-31`); the governing prose is `basic-lib/convenience.tex`, found by grepping the prose chapters (§3).

The declarations belong in the library, not in the compiler. `grep -rn` over `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler` and `runtimeSystem` for `Option`, `Some`, `None` and `NoneObject` finds nothing, so the protocol this copies is special-cased nowhere in Java or Scala; and `WellKnownNames.java:114-115` makes `CompilerLibrary` and `CompilerBuiltin` the compile path's implicit prelude, so a declaration in either is in scope for every compiled program. This rung therefore touches no `.java` and no `.scala`, and needs no `ant compileAll`.

Within the library, the choice was `Library/CompilerLibrary` (where the team's draft sits) over `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin` (where `Option` sits). The draft's location was followed. It works: `CompilerLibrary` already declares objects that extend a trait declared in `CompilerBuiltin` (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:66-103`, thirteen objects extending `UncheckedException`, which is `CompilerBuiltin.fsi:711`), which is exactly what `Maybe extends Condition[\T\]` needs, and the coercion works from there (§5). It also costs less to rebuild: editing `CompilerLibrary` rebuilds three components (41 s + 2 s + 2 s measured), editing `CompilerBuiltin` would rebuild five (145 s measured cold).

## 3. Precedent search: has the team solved this here already, and in how many ways

Four ways, and they do not all agree.

1. **The interpreter's prelude.** `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1306-1364`: `value trait Maybe[\T\] extends { AnyMaybe, Condition[\T\], UniqueItem[\T\] } comprises { Nothing[\T\], Just[\T\] }`, `value object Just[\T\](x:T)` at `:1312`, `value object Nothing[\T\]` at `:1341`, `value trait AnyMaybe` at `:1292`, api at `.fsi:829-880`. The empty case is **parametric**, and the source says so under protest: `FortressLibrary.fss:1339-1340` "Obviously ought to be a non-parametric singleton when we get where clauses working", repeated in the api at `.fsi:857-858`.
2. **The team's draft for this world**, commented out at `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229`: `value trait Maybe[\T\] extends Condition[\T\] comprises { Just[\T\], NothingObject[\T\] }` with `coerce(x: Nothing)`, `value object Just[\T\](x:T)`, `value object NothingObject[\T\]` with a second `coerce(x: Nothing)`, and `object Nothing end`. The empty case is **non-parametric plus a per-`T` object joined by a coercion**.
3. **The team's tests of that draft**, all in `ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/` and gated by nothing (`explorations/coordinator/map/test-coverage.md:32`): `MaybeTest1.fss:22-83`, `MaybeTest2.fss:29-`, `GenTest3.fss:29-41`, `GenTest4.fss:423-454`, `HelperTest1.fss:231-298` and its two copies — six components, all with `NothingObject[\T\]` and a separate `Nothing`, i.e. shape 2. `GenTest4.fss:454` writes it `value object Nothing end`; `MaybeTest1.fss:83` and `HelperTest1.fss:298` write `object Nothing end`.
4. **The shipped `Option`**, `CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649-661` and `.fss:1308-1367`: shape 2 exactly, under the names `Option`, `Some`, `NoneObject`, `None`, complete, compiled into every program's prelude, and the only one of the four that is known to work. Nothing in the gated corpora names it (`grep -rn` over `compiler_tests/`, `other_compiler_tests/`, `library_tests/` finds only the English word "None" in three `Compiled12.*` files), so `probes/OptionCoercion.fss` was written to measure it before copying it. It compiles, links and runs: `probes/OptionCoercion.txt` records `empty=None full=Some(7)` / `PASS` for `empty: Option[\ZZ32\] = None`.

The corpus is a fifth voice but not a solution: every one of the 80 uses of the name in `ProjectFortress/tests/` and the `*_tests/` directories writes the parametric `Nothing[\T\]` (22 files; 15 of them in `tests/`), and so do `Library/List.fss` (4), `Set.fss` (6), `Map.fss` (11), `PureList.fss` (6) and `QuickCheck.fss`/`.fsi` — the interpreter-world library the later library route would port. There is no use of an unparameterised `Nothing` as a value anywhere in the tree outside shapes 2 and 3.

Shape 4 was copied, member for member, because it is the one that runs, and the names were taken from shape 2, because it is the team's decision for this world and it agrees with the specification (§4).

## 4. The decision

**The specification's spelling of the empty case was taken, not the corpus's.** `Maybe[\T\] comprises { Just[\T\], NothingObject[\T\] }` with `coerce(_: Nothing) = NothingObject[\T\]` and a separate `value object Nothing end`. This was a decision; it was not forced by the code.

The two candidates cannot coexist. `Nothing` is one name: either it is a non-parametric object, in which case `Nothing[\ZZ32\]` is a static error, or it is a parametric one, in which case a bare `Nothing` has no static argument to take. A same-name overload of the two is not merely unprecedented but unwritable: the coercion's parameter type has to name the singleton's type, and if a parametric object shares the name then the bare type name `Nothing` does not resolve to the singleton. So the fork is binary.

**What the specification says.** `basic-lib/convenience.tex:46-55` is a prose chapter of Part Basic Library, not an api rendering, and it declares the empty case as one object: `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}`. `basic/exceptions.tex:122,124` then uses it the way a non-parametric singleton is used, `getter message(): Maybe[\String\] = Nothing`. Two independent prose passages, and they agree.

**Why the specification's own text cannot be transcribed.** The declaration depends on a `where` clause, and the compile path refuses one on an object declaration: `CodeGen.java:4088`, in `forObjectDeclPrePass`, admits a declaration only if `header.getWhereClause().isNone()`, otherwise `sayWhat`. `probes/WhereClauseNothing.fss` is the specification's declaration under local names, and `probes/WhereClauseNothing.txt` records what happens to it. The compensating mechanism is coercion, which this path has and the interpreter does not (`explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:288`: "nothing: no occurrence of `Coercion` or `coerce` anywhere under `interpreter/`"). That is precisely why the team's draft for this world spells the empty case as it does, and why the interpreter's prelude does not: the interpreter had no way to write it.

**What the corpus says, and what it costs to overrule it.** Overruling it costs this rung both of the two ladder files `CLIMB-BATCH-1.md` names for it. `ExceptionScoping.fss:31` writes `Nothing[\ZZ32\].get` and `oddJuxt.fss:22,24` write `Nothing[\ZZ32\]`; both now fail with "Unexpected type for a singleton object reference" instead of "Function Nothing is not defined" (§7). Neither passes. The cascade the rung was chosen for is unaffected, because it runs on `Maybe` in type position and `Just(x)` in expression position, which both spellings serve: `HeapTest.fss` and `IntMapTest.fss` lose "Maybe is undefined" and move to their next wall, and `maybeTest.fss` and `naturalsTest.fss` move past `Nothing` and `Just` to `NOTIN` and `__cond` (§7).

**The alternative and its cost.** Taking the corpus's `Nothing[\T\]` would clear `ExceptionScoping.fss` and `oddJuxt.fss` now and would spare the later library route 27 renames in `List.fss`, `Set.fss`, `Map.fss` and `PureList.fss`. Its cost is that `= Nothing`, the only spelling of a `Maybe` value the prose chapters ever write, would be a static error in the compiler world for good, and the compiler world would be carrying the interpreter's acknowledged workaround for a feature the compiler world does not need the workaround for — it has coercion. The library route is a reserved fork and those files will be rewritten line by line when it opens; `basic-lib/convenience.tex` will not be rewritten. Two ladder files, whose spelling the specification does not sanction, were judged the smaller loss, and they are not lost silently: they become ledger row 329 (§8), which names the spelling, both probes and where the fix lies.

**A second decision, smaller: beside `Option`, not over it.** `Maybe` is a second copy of the `Condition` protocol rather than built on `Option`. Three ways to build it over `Option` were considered. Making `Maybe[\T\]` extend `Option[\T\]` fails because `Option` is declared `comprises { NoneObject[\E19\], Some[\E19\] }` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:650`) and a `comprises` clause is closed, so it would have to be widened — a change to a declared type the prelude already has, which `CLIMB-BATCH-1.md` reserves as a stop. Making `Just`/`NothingObject` wrap a `Some`/`NoneObject` field would put an indirection and an allocation under every method to save one-line bodies. A type alias is not available (`Specification/fortress/preamble.tex:55-96` lists type aliases among the not-yet-supported features). The copy costs 56 lines of one-line bodies in `CompilerLibrary.fss`; that was judged cheaper than any of the three, and it is also what the team's draft does — its `Maybe` extends `Condition[\T\]`, not `Option`.

**A third, smaller still: the commented draft was replaced, not left beside the live code.** `CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229` now holds the live declarations in place of the comment. Leaving the comment beside working declarations of the same names would be a stale second answer in the source, and `explorations/protocol.md` keeps rationale out of the tree. The draft is quoted in full in §3 of this report, so nothing is lost.

## 5. What changed

`Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-235` — the commented draft replaced by live declarations: `value trait Maybe[\T extends Any\] extends { Condition[\T\] } comprises { Just[\T\], NothingObject[\T\] }` with `coerce(_: Nothing)`, `getter isNothing(): Boolean`, `seq(): Maybe[\T\]`, `abstract filter(...)` and a commented `opr SQCAP`; `value object Just[\T extends Any\](x: T)`; `value object NothingObject[\T extends Any\]`; `value object Nothing end`.

`Library/CompilerLibrary.fss:522-582` — the bodies, inserted before the "Making vectors" section so the component's order matches the api's. Member for member the bodies of `Option`, `Some` and `NoneObject` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:1308-1367`) with `Option` replaced by `Maybe`, `Some` by `Just`, `NoneObject` by `NothingObject`, `None` by `Nothing`, plus `getter isNothing(): Boolean = NOT self.holds` in the trait.

`ProjectFortress/library_tests/MaybeRungM.fss`, `MaybeRungM.test` — the test.

## 6. Deviations

1. The specification's single `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] ... where {T extends Object}` (`convenience.tex:49`) becomes `value object NothingObject[\T\] extends Maybe[\T\]` plus `value object Nothing end` plus `coerce(_: Nothing) = NothingObject[\T\]`, because `CodeGen.java:4088` refuses a where clause on an object. Semantics preserved at all three use sites the specification writes (§7, `probes/MaybeCoercionSites.txt`); the spelling `Nothing[\T\]` is not preserved (row 329).
2. The specification writes `object`, this writes `value object`, for `Maybe`, `Just`, `NothingObject` and `Nothing` alike — following `Option` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649-661`), the interpreter (`FortressLibrary.fss:1306-1341`) and the draft (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229`), all three of which make the type a value type. The draft writes plain `object Nothing end`; `value object None end` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:661`) and the team's `GenTest4.fss:454` write `value`, and `value` was taken.
3. The specification's `object Just[\T\](just: T)` names the field `just`; this names it `x`, after `value object Some[\E20\](x: E20)` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:657`), the draft's `Just[\T\](x:T)` (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:223`) and the interpreter's `Just[\T\](x:T)` (`FortressLibrary.fss:1312`). Three precedents against one, and the field is not read by name from outside.
4. The specification's `isNothing: Boolean` is a field declaration in a trait; this writes `getter isNothing(): Boolean`, the form every member of `Condition` and `Option` is written in (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:622-655`) and the form `exceptions.tex:122` itself expands the `settable message: Maybe[\String\]` of `:68` into.
5. `Maybe` extends `Condition[\T\]`, which `convenience.tex:46` does not; the draft (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:217`), the interpreter (`FortressLibrary.fss:1307`) and `Option` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649`) all do, and it is what makes a `for` over a `Maybe` work.
6. The specification's `excludes Just[\T\]` on `Nothing` is not written, and neither is any `excludes` clause; `Option` has none either (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649-661`), and the exclusion is implied by the closed `comprises` clause.
7. `opr SQCAP` is declared as a comment, not live — as on `Option` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:652`) and in the draft (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:220`). It is the interpreter's semilattice meet (`FortressLibrary.fss:1309`); no prose chapter declares it on `Maybe` (`grep -rn SQCAP Specification/basic/ Specification/basic-lib/ Specification/advanced-lib/` finds it only as an operator parameter in `advanced-lib/algebraic-constraints.tex`), and `library_tests/MaybeTest9.fss:64-68` has the team's own `SQCAP` assertions commented out.
8. The coercion is declared once, on the trait; the draft declares it twice, on the trait at `CompilerLibrary.fsi:219` and again on `NothingObject` at `:227`. `Option` declares it once (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:651`), and once is what works.
9. `AnyMaybe` (`FortressLibrary.fss:1292`) is not declared, and neither are `UniqueItem`/`NotUnique` (`:1375-1391`). Rung 2 already recorded that the compiler world has no referent for `AnyMaybe` when it ported `HasRank` (`CompilerLibrary.fss:549-551`); `Library/Set.fsi:65` will need it when the library route opens, and that is that fork's work, not this rung's.

## 7. Recorded failure, recorded pass and the differentials
